A knight in armor rides calmly through a dark valley while Death with an hourglass and a horned Devil follow behind him. Albrecht Dürer made this engraving in 1513, and its themes of death and courage echo the fears of the plague years.

A dying miser lies in bed while Death stands in the doorway and a demon tempts him with a bag of money. Hieronymus Bosch painted this around 1500 to show how nothing can be taken to the grave, a popular message after the long years of plague.

Christ appoints Saint Roch as the protector of plague victims, a saint who was believed to have cared for the sick during an epidemic. Peter Paul Rubens painted it in 1619 for a church in Antwerp, where people prayed to Saint Roch in times of plague.

The Parthenon, the temple built in the golden age of Athens in the 400s BC, stands in golden light on the Acropolis. Frederic Church, the American painter of grand landscapes, visited Greece in 1869 and painted it in 1871.
Vasily Polenov, a Russian painter, shows the ruined Parthenon standing high above Athens, the temple Pericles built in the golden age. He visited Greece in the early 1880s and painted it in 1881.
